definitions.explanation: A widely used vegetable in Japanese cooking with tightly packed, pale green to white leaves. A staple ingredient in hot pot dishes ({鍋|なべ}), stir-fries, pickles, and soups, especially popular in winter.

examples.japanese: {鍋|なべ}に{白菜|はくさい}を{入|い}れた。
examples.english: I put Chinese cabbage in the hot pot.

examples.japanese: {冬|ふゆ}は{白菜|はくさい}が{甘|あま}くなって{美味|おい}しい。
examples.english: In winter, Chinese cabbage becomes sweet and delicious.

examples.japanese: {白菜|はくさい}と{豚肉|ぶたにく}のミルフィーユ{鍋|なべ}は、{材料|ざいりょう}を{交互|こうご}に{重|かさ}ねるだけで{簡単|かんたん}に{作|つく}れる{人気|にんき}レシピだ。
examples.english: Mille-feuille hot pot with Chinese cabbage and pork is a popular recipe that can be made easily by just layering the ingredients alternately.

notes:
USAGE:
One of the most common vegetables in Japanese home cooking, especially during the colder months. {白菜|はくさい} is the quintessential {鍋|なべ} (hot pot) ingredient and is also widely used for {漬物|つけもの} (pickles). The Korean equivalent, kimchi (キムチ), also uses this vegetable.

ETYMOLOGY:
Literally "white vegetable" — {白|はく} (white) + {菜|さい} (vegetable). Named for the white stems and pale inner leaves.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {白菜|はくさい}の{漬物|つけもの}: Chinese cabbage pickles
- {白菜|はくさい}{鍋|なべ}: Chinese cabbage hot pot
- {白菜|はくさい}を{切|き}る: cut Chinese cabbage
- {白菜|はくさい}キムチ: Chinese cabbage kimchi
